questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Dogra dynasty' ruled Jammu & Kashmir from 1846 until:
questions.explanation: The Dogra dynasty ruled from the Treaty of Amritsar (1846) until India's independence and accession (1947) when Maharaja Hari Singh signed the Instrument of Accession. '1952' is wrong — by then J&K had an elected government. '1950' is wrong — Constitution came into effect but Dogra rule ended in 1947. '1939' is wrong — Dogras still ruled then.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Jammu & Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019:

(i) The state of J&K was bifurcated into two Union Territories.
(ii) J&K UT has a Legislative Assembly while Ladakh UT does not.
(iii) The Lt. Governor is the administrator for both UTs.
(iv) All Central laws now apply directly to both J&K and Ladakh.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Two UTs created (i correct). J&K has legislature, Ladakh doesn't (ii correct). Lt. Governors administer both (iii correct). Central laws apply directly post-abrogation of Art. 370 (iv correct). '(i), (ii) and (iii) only' excludes (iv). '(i) and (ii) only' excludes (iii) and (iv). '(ii), (iii) and (iv) only' excludes (i).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Kashmir Valley receives heavy snowfall during winter.
Reason (R): The Pir Panjal range blocks the cold northwesterly winds and forces them to shed moisture as snow over the Valley.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct
questions.explanation: Kashmir does receive heavy winter snow (A correct). However, R is wrong — winter precipitation in Kashmir comes from WESTERN DISTURBANCES from the Mediterranean/Caspian region, not blocked northwesterly winds. The Pir Panjal range is on the southern side and doesn't block cold NW winds in the way described. 'Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)' is wrong because R misstates the mechanism. 'Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)' is wrong because R is incorrect. '(A) is not correct but (R) is correct' is wrong because A is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following passes in J&K/Ladakh with their significance:

Column I:
(a) Zoji La
(b) Banihal Pass
(c) Khardung La
(d) Pir Panjal Pass

Column II:
(i) Connects Leh to Nubra Valley
(ii) Connects Kashmir Valley to Ladakh on NH-1
(iii) Connects Jammu to Kashmir Valley on NH-44
(iv) Historical pass on the Mughal Road

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Zoji La connects Kashmir to Ladakh on NH-1 (ii). Banihal connects Jammu to Kashmir on NH-44 (iii). Khardung La connects Leh to Nubra Valley (i). Pir Panjal Pass is on the historic Mughal Road (iv). '(a)-(iii), (b)-(ii), (c)-(iv), (d)-(i)' swaps (a) and (b). '(a)-(ii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(iii)' swaps (b) and (d). '(a)-(i), (b)-(iii), (c)-(ii), (d)-(iv)' swaps (a) and (c).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following wildlife sanctuaries/national parks are located in J&K?

(i) Dachigam National Park
(ii) Kishtwar National Park
(iii) Overa-Aru Wildlife Sanctuary
(iv) Hemis National Park

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Dachigam (Srinagar) protects Hangul deer (i correct). Kishtwar NP in Jammu division (ii correct). Overa-Aru in Anantnag (iv correct). Hemis National Park (iv) is wrong — it is in LADAKH UT, not J&K UT. '(i), (ii), (iv) and (iii)' includes (iv). '(i) and (ii) only' excludes (iii). '(ii), (iv) and (iii) only' includes (iv).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Hangul' (Kashmir Stag) is primarily found in which national park?
questions.explanation: The Hangul (Cervus hanglu) is found primarily in Dachigam NP near Srinagar. 'Kishtwar NP' is wrong — it's home to snow leopards and Himalayan brown bear. 'Hemis NP' is wrong — famous for snow leopards in Ladakh. 'Salim Ali NP' is wrong — it's a bird sanctuary in Srinagar.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the history of J&K:

(i) The first Mughal Emperor to visit Kashmir was Babur.
(ii) Kalhana wrote the Rajatarangini in the 12th century.
(iii) Sultan Zain-ul-Abidin is known as 'Budshah' for his religious tolerance.
(iv) The Sikh rule in Kashmir lasted from 1819 to 1846.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Kalhana wrote Rajatarangini c.1148-50 (i correct). Zain-ul-Abidin was Budshah (ii correct). Sikh rule 1819-1846 (iii correct). (i) is wrong because Akbar was the first Mughal to visit Kashmir (1589), not Babur. '(ii), (iii), (iv) and (i)' includes (i). '(ii) and (iii) only' excludes (iv). '(iii), (iv) and (i) only' includes (i).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Nishat Bagh' in Srinagar was built by:
questions.explanation: Nishat Bagh ('Garden of Joy') was built by Asaf Khan, the elder brother of Nur Jahan, in 1633. 'Jahangir' is wrong — he built Shalimar Bagh. 'Shah Jahan' is wrong — he added to gardens but didn't build Nishat. 'Akbar' is wrong — he preceded Nishat's construction.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Chenab river has multiple major hydroelectric projects in J&K.
Reason (R): The Chenab flows through deep, narrow gorges in the mountainous terrain of Jammu division, providing high hydraulic head ideal for power generation.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Chenab has Salal, Baglihar, Dulhasti, Pakal Dul etc. (A correct). Its deep gorges in mountainous terrain create high head for hydropower (R correct and explains why so many projects are on this river). 'Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)' is wrong because R directly explains A. '(A) is correct but (R) is not correct' is wrong because R is correct. '(A) is not correct but (R) is correct' is wrong because A is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Line of Control' (LoC) in J&K was established after which agreement?
questions.explanation: The LoC replaced the Ceasefire Line after the Simla Agreement of 1972 between India and Pakistan. 'Tashkent Agreement' is wrong — that ended the 1965 war but didn't create the LoC. 'Karachi Agreement' is wrong — that established the original Ceasefire Line. 'Lahore Declaration' is wrong — that was a peace initiative, not about the LoC.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following J&K districts with their famous products/associations:

Column I:
(a) Pulwama
(b) Kupwara
(c) Kathua
(d) Kishtwar

Column II:
(i) Saffron cultivation
(ii) Sapphire mining
(iii) Basohli painting tradition
(iv) Walnut production

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Pulwama/Pampore area is famous for saffron (i). Kupwara is a major walnut-producing district (iv). Kathua has the Basohli painting tradition (iii). Kishtwar is known for sapphire mining (Paddar area) (ii). '(a)-(iv), (b)-(i), (c)-(ii), (d)-(iii)' swaps (a) and (b). '(a)-(i), (b)-(iii), (c)-(iv), (d)-(ii)' swaps (b) and (c). '(a)-(ii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(iii), (d)-(i)' swaps (a) and (d).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Bahu Fort' in Jammu is believed to have been built by:
questions.explanation: Bahu Fort is traditionally believed to have been built by Raja Bahulochan, the founder of Jammu city, over 3,000 years ago. 'Gulab Singh' is wrong — Dogra era was much later. 'Akbar' is wrong — Mughal emperor who visited Kashmir. 'Amar Singh' is wrong — later Dogra ruler.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the economy of J&K:

(i) Tourism contributes significantly to J&K's GDP.
(ii) J&K has extensive coal mining operations.
(iii) J&K is India's largest producer of walnuts.
(iv) Handicrafts like Pashmina, carpet weaving, and papier-mâché are major cottage industries.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Tourism is vital to J&K economy (i correct). J&K dominates India's walnut production (ii correct). Pashmina/carpets/papier-mâché are significant industries (iii correct). (ii) is wrong — J&K does NOT have extensive coal mining; it has limited mineral resources and no significant coal deposits. '(i), (iii), (iv) and (ii)' includes (ii). '(i) and (iv) only' excludes (iii). '(iii), (iv) and (ii) only' includes (ii).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Mughal Gardens' of Kashmir include Shalimar Bagh, Nishat Bagh, and:
questions.explanation: The three famous Mughal Gardens of Srinagar are Shalimar Bagh, Nishat Bagh, and Chashme Shahi (Royal Spring). 'Tulip Garden' is wrong — it's modern (2007), not Mughal era. 'Botanical Garden' is wrong — not a Mughal garden. 'Achabal Garden' is wrong — while Mughal-era, it's in Anantnag and not traditionally grouped with the three Srinagar gardens.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Jhelum river is crucial to the agriculture of the Kashmir Valley.
Reason (R): The Jhelum and its tributaries provide irrigation water to the rice paddies and other crops of the flat valley floor.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Jhelum is vital for Kashmir agriculture (A correct). Its tributaries irrigate the valley floor for rice and crops (R correct and explains how the river supports agriculture). 'Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)' is wrong because R explains the mechanism. '(A) is correct but (R) is not correct' is wrong because R is correct. '(A) is not correct but (R) is correct' is wrong because A is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The total number of districts in J&K UT (as of 2024) is:
questions.explanation: J&K UT has 20 districts — 10 each in Kashmir and Jammu divisions. '22' is wrong — includes Ladakh districts. '18' is wrong — fewer than actual. '24' is wrong — too many.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are traditional festivals celebrated in J&K?

(i) Lohri — celebrated in Jammu region
(ii) Shivratri — celebrated as 'Herath' by Kashmiri Pandits
(iii) Onam — harvest festival of Kashmir
(iv) Eid-ul-Fitr — marking end of Ramadan

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Lohri is celebrated in Jammu (i correct). Shivratri as Herath is important for Kashmiri Pandits (ii correct). Eid-ul-Fitr is celebrated by the Muslim majority (iii correct). (iii) is wrong because Onam is a festival of KERALA, not Kashmir. '(i), (ii), (iv) and (iii)' includes (iii). '(i) and (iv) only' excludes (ii). '(ii), (iv) and (iii) only' includes (iii).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Raghunath Temple' in Jammu was built during the reign of:
options: Maharaja Gulab Singh and Maharaja Ranbir Singh
questions.correctAnswer: Maharaja Gulab Singh and Maharaja Ranbir Singh
questions.explanation: Raghunath Temple was started by Maharaja Gulab Singh (1835-57) and completed by his son Maharaja Ranbir Singh. 'Akbar' is wrong — Mughal emperor, didn't build Hindu temples in Jammu. 'Sheikh Abdullah' is wrong — political leader, not temple builder. 'Raja Amar Singh' is wrong — later Dogra ruler.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following lakes with their locations in J&K:

Column I:
(a) Dal Lake
(b) Mansar Lake
(c) Wular Lake
(d) Sheshnag Lake

Column II:
(i) Anantnag (on Amarnath route)
(ii) Srinagar
(iii) Bandipora
(iv) Jammu (Udhampur road)

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Dal Lake is in Srinagar (ii). Mansar Lake is near Jammu/Udhampur (iv). Wular Lake is in Bandipora (iii). Sheshnag is on the Amarnath route from Anantnag side (i). '(a)-(iv), (b)-(ii), (c)-(i), (d)-(iii)' swaps (a) and (b). '(a)-(ii), (b)-(iii), (c)-(iv), (d)-(i)' swaps (b) and (c). '(a)-(i), (b)-(iv), (c)-(iii), (d)-(ii)' swaps (a) and (d).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Peer Budhan' area in Poonch district is associated with:
options: A religious shrine and historical battlefield site
questions.correctAnswer: A religious shrine and historical battlefield site
questions.explanation: Peer Budhan is a significant religious site and was a key location during Indo-Pak conflicts. 'Saffron cultivation' is wrong — that's Pampore/Pulwama. 'Walnut plantations' is wrong — more common in Kupwara/Shopian. 'Thermal power plant' is wrong — no such facility there.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about transport in J&K:

(i) The Jammu-Srinagar National Highway (NH-44) passes through the Jawahar Tunnel.
(ii) The USBRL, completed in June 2025, is regarded as one of India's most challenging railway projects.
(iii) The Anantnag-Qazigund section of the railway is operational.
(iv) Srinagar has the only airport in J&K with international status.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — NH-44 crosses the Pir Panjal range through the Jawahar Tunnel at Banihal. (ii) is correct — the 272 km USBRL, with 36 tunnels and around 943 bridges, was inaugurated on 6 June 2025 and is widely described as one of the hardest railway projects India has built. (iii) is correct — the Anantnag-Qazigund section was among the earliest stretches commissioned. (iv) is wrong because Jammu airport also carries international status, so Srinagar is not the only one. The remaining options each either include (iv) or drop a correct statement.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The famous 'Pashmina' shawl is made from the wool of the __________ goat.
questions.explanation: Pashmina comes from the undercoat of the Changthangi goat found in Ladakh's Changthang plateau. 'Angora' is wrong — that's from Angora rabbits. 'Cashmere' is wrong — while related, the specific J&K breed is Changthangi. 'Merino' is wrong — that's a sheep breed for regular wool.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Amarnath Cave is one of the holiest Hindu shrines in India.
Reason (R): A natural ice stalagmite forms in the cave annually, believed to be a Shiva Lingam, attracting lakhs of pilgrims during Shravan month.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Amarnath is among India's holiest shrines (A correct). The natural ice Lingam forms annually and draws pilgrims (R correct and explains why it's sacred). 'Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)' is wrong because R directly explains A's significance. '(A) is correct but (R) is not correct' is wrong because R is correct. '(A) is not correct but (R) is correct' is wrong because A is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Tawi river' flows through which major city of J&K?
questions.explanation: The Tawi river flows through Jammu city and is its lifeline. 'Srinagar' is wrong — Jhelum flows through it. 'Udhampur' is wrong — Devika river flows there. 'Kathua' is wrong — different rivers.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the 'Vaishno Devi' pilgrimage:

(i) The shrine is located in Srinagar district.
(ii) The shrine is located in the Trikuta Mountains at about 5,200 feet elevation.
(iii) It is managed by the Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Shrine Board (SMVDSB).
(iv) The pilgrimage trek starts from the base camp at Katra.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Located in Trikuta Mountains at ~5,200 ft (i correct). SMVDSB manages it (ii correct). Trek starts from Katra (iii correct). (i) is wrong — Vaishno Devi is in REASI district (earlier in Jammu district), not Srinagar. '(ii), (iii), (iv) and (i)' includes (i). '(ii) and (iv) only' excludes (iii). '(iii), (iv) and (i) only' includes (i).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following historical rulers/periods with their contributions to J&K:

Column I:
(a) Lalitaditya Muktapida
(b) Sikh period (1819-1846)
(c) Dogra period (1846-1947)
(d) Sultan Shah Mir

Column II:
(i) Founded the first Muslim dynasty of Kashmir (1339)
(ii) Built the Martand Sun Temple
(iii) Established modern governance and infrastructure
(iv) Ended Afghan rule in Kashmir

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Lalitaditya built Martand Temple (ii). Sikhs under Ranjit Singh ended Afghan rule (iv). Dogras modernized governance (iii). Shah Mir founded first Muslim dynasty 1339 (i). '(a)-(iv), (b)-(ii), (c)-(i), (d)-(iii)' swaps (a) and (b). '(a)-(ii), (b)-(iii), (c)-(iv), (d)-(i)' swaps (b) and (c). '(a)-(i), (b)-(iv), (c)-(iii), (d)-(ii)' swaps (a) and (d).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
The following data shows tourist arrivals (in lakhs) in J&K:

2021 → 67
2022 → 189
2023 → 210

What is the percentage increase from 2021 to 2023?
questions.explanation: Increase = 210-67 = 143. Percentage = (143/67)×100 ≈ 213.4%. '182%' is wrong — would need increase of 122. '150%' is wrong — would need increase of 100.5. '250%' is wrong — would need increase of 167.5.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Mubarak Mandi Palace' is a significant heritage complex located in:
questions.explanation: Mubarak Mandi Palace complex in Jammu was the royal residence of the Dogra kings. 'Srinagar' is wrong — Srinagar has Hari Parbat Fort. 'Rajouri' is wrong — no such palace there. 'Anantnag' is wrong — different district.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): J&K is famous for its handicraft industry.
Reason (R): The cold winters of Kashmir historically kept artisans indoors, leading to the development of intricate handcraft skills like Pashmina weaving, carpet making, and wood carving.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: J&K is renowned for handicrafts (A correct). Long cold winters drove indoor artisanal work, developing these skills over generations (R correct and explains the historical reason for handicraft prominence). 'Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)' is wrong because R provides the historical explanation. '(A) is correct but (R) is not correct' is wrong because R is a valid explanation. '(A) is not correct but (R) is correct' is wrong because A is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Pir Panjal Railway Tunnel' on the USBRL project is approximately:
questions.explanation: The Pir Panjal (T-80) tunnel at 11.2 km is India's longest railway tunnel. '5 km' is wrong — far too short. '15 km' is wrong — longer than actual. '8 km' is wrong — underestimate.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following languages spoken in J&K are included in the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution?

(i) Kashmiri
(ii) Gojri
(iii) Dogri
(iv) Urdu

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Kashmiri (i correct), Dogri (ii correct, added in 2003), and Urdu (iv correct) are in the Eighth Schedule. Gojri (ii) is wrong — it is NOT included in the Eighth Schedule despite being widely spoken by Gujjar/Bakerwal communities. '(i), (iii), (ii) and (iv)' includes (ii). '(i) and (iii) only' excludes (iv). '(iii), (ii) and (iv) only' includes (ii).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Lal Chowk' in Srinagar is significant because:
options: It is the commercial and political centre of Srinagar city
It is a famous temple complex
It is the site of Dal Lake
It is the location of the international airport
questions.correctAnswer: It is the commercial and political centre of Srinagar city
questions.explanation: Lal Chowk is Srinagar's main commercial hub and has political significance (clock tower). 'Temple complex' is wrong — it's a commercial area. 'Site of Dal Lake' is wrong — Dal Lake is elsewhere in Srinagar. 'Airport location' is wrong — airport is in Budgam area.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Kashmir silk industry:

(i) Sericulture (silk worm rearing) is practiced in parts of J&K.
(ii) Mulberry cultivation supports the silk industry in Kashmir.
(iii) J&K is the largest silk-producing state in India.
(iv) The silk carpets of Kashmir are world-famous.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Sericulture is practiced in J&K (i correct). Mulberry trees support it (ii correct). Silk carpets of Kashmir are internationally renowned (iii correct). (iii) is wrong because Karnataka is India's largest silk producer, not J&K. '(i), (ii), (iv) and (iii)' includes (iii). '(i) and (iv) only' excludes (ii). '(ii), (iv) and (iii) only' includes (iii).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The __________ is the highest civilian award of J&K UT.
options: There is no separate J&K civilian award post-2019 (national awards apply)
questions.correctAnswer: There is no separate J&K civilian award post-2019 (national awards apply)
questions.explanation: After the J&K Reorganisation Act 2019, national awards like Padma awards apply directly to J&K UT — there is no separate state civilian award system. 'Sher-e-Kashmir Award' is wrong — while it existed historically under state government, it's not current. 'J&K Ratna' is wrong — no such award exists. 'Budshah Award' is wrong — fictional name.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following towns with the rivers they are situated on:

Column I:
(a) Srinagar
(b) Jammu
(c) Anantnag
(d) Kishtwar

Column II:
(i) Chenab
(ii) Jhelum
(iii) Tawi
(iv) Lidder (tributary of Jhelum)

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Srinagar on Jhelum (ii). Jammu on Tawi (iii). Anantnag on Lidder (iv). Kishtwar on Chenab (i). '(a)-(iii), (b)-(ii), (c)-(i), (d)-(iv)' swaps (a) and (b). '(a)-(ii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(iii), (d)-(i)' swaps (b) and (c). '(a)-(i), (b)-(iii), (c)-(iv), (d)-(ii)' swaps (a) and (d).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Gurez Valley' in Bandipora district is famous for:
options: Its pristine natural beauty and the Kishanganga river flowing through it
questions.correctAnswer: Its pristine natural beauty and the Kishanganga river flowing through it
questions.explanation: Gurez Valley is known for its stunning natural beauty, the Kishanganga river, and Habba Khatoon peak. 'Apple orchards' is wrong — while some exist, it's not what Gurez is famous for. 'Coal mining' is wrong — no mining there. 'Thermal power' is wrong — no such facility.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Indus Waters Treaty allows India limited use of western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab).
Reason (R): India can build run-of-river hydroelectric projects on these rivers with certain restrictions on storage capacity.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: IWT allows India limited use of western rivers (A correct). Run-of-river projects with storage restrictions are permitted (R correct and describes the specific type of allowed use). 'Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)' is wrong because R explains what 'limited use' means. '(A) is correct but (R) is not correct' is wrong because R is correct. '(A) is not correct but (R) is correct' is wrong because A is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Shankaracharya Hill' temple in Srinagar is also known by which name?
questions.explanation: Shankaracharya temple sits atop the hill called Takht-e-Sulaiman (Throne of Solomon). 'Hari Parbat' is wrong — that's a different hill with a fort. 'Koh-e-Maran' is wrong — that's another hill in Srinagar. 'Mahadev Peak' is wrong — not the name.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following crops are primarily grown in the Jammu region of J&K?

(i) Basmati rice
(ii) Wheat
(iii) Maize
(iv) Saffron

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Basmati rice (R.S. Pura belt) (i correct), wheat (rabi crop) (ii correct), and maize (kharif) (iii correct) are grown in Jammu region. (iv) is wrong because saffron is grown in the KASHMIR Valley (Pampore), not Jammu. '(i), (ii), (iii) and (iv)' includes (iv). '(i) and (ii) only' excludes (iii). '(ii), (iii) and (iv) only' includes (iv).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Patnitop' hill station is located in which district?
questions.explanation: Patnitop is in Udhampur district on the Jammu-Srinagar highway at ~2,024 m. 'Doda' is wrong — different district further north. 'Kishtwar' is wrong — mountainous district in Chenab valley. 'Ramban' is wrong — transit district on NH-44.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Instrument of Accession (1947):

(i) It was signed unconditionally with no special provisions.
(ii) It was signed by Maharaja Hari Singh on 26 October 1947.
(iii) It covered Defence, External Affairs, and Communications.
(iv) It made J&K a part of independent India.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Signed 26 Oct 1947 (i correct). Covered Defence/External Affairs/Communications (ii correct). Made J&K part of India (iii correct). (i) is wrong — the accession was conditional with Article 370 providing special autonomous status to J&K. '(ii), (iii), (iv) and (i)' includes (i). '(ii) and (iv) only' excludes (iii). '(iii), (iv) and (i) only' includes (i).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
The following data shows the installed capacity of power projects on the Chenab river:

Salal → 690
Baglihar-I → 450
Dulhasti → 390
Uri-I → 480
Kishanganga → 330

Which project in the table is NOT on the Chenab river?
questions.explanation: Uri-I is on the Jhelum river (not Chenab) and Kishanganga is on the Kishanganga/Neelum river (not Chenab). Salal, Baglihar-I, and Dulhasti are all on the Chenab. 'Salal only' is wrong — it IS on Chenab. 'Baglihar-I only' is wrong — it IS on Chenab. 'Dulhasti only' is wrong — it IS on Chenab.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The __________ is the state animal of J&K.
questions.explanation: The Hangul (Cervus hanglu) is J&K's state animal, found mainly in Dachigam NP. 'Snow Leopard' is wrong — it's Ladakh's state animal. 'Himalayan Brown Bear' is wrong — while found in J&K, it's not the state animal. 'Markhor' is wrong — it's found in small numbers but isn't the state animal.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Basohli' school of painting originated in which region of J&K?
questions.explanation: Basohli painting (miniature style, 17th century) originated in Basohli town, Kathua district. 'Srinagar' is wrong — different artistic tradition. 'Anantnag' is wrong — south Kashmir. 'Baramulla' is wrong — north Kashmir.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): J&K's economy is heavily dependent on horticulture.
Reason (R): The apple industry alone accounts for approximately 7-8% of J&K's GDP and provides livelihood to millions in the Valley.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: J&K economy depends heavily on horticulture (A correct). Apple alone contributes ~7-8% of GDP and employs millions (R correct and demonstrates the 'heavy dependence' mentioned in A). 'Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)' is wrong because R quantifies and explains A's claim. '(A) is correct but (R) is not correct' is wrong because R is correct. '(A) is not correct but (R) is correct' is wrong because A is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Gujjar' and 'Bakerwal' communities in J&K are primarily:
questions.explanation: Gujjars and Bakerwals are traditional nomadic herders who migrate seasonally with livestock. 'Urban traders' is wrong — they're rural/pastoral. 'Rice farmers' is wrong — they're herders. 'Government officials' is wrong — they're a tribal community, not an official designation.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following administrative features with their descriptions:

Column I:
(a) Darbar Move
(b) District Development Council
(c) Lt. Governor
(d) Divisional Commissioner

Column II:
(i) Head of administration of J&K UT
(ii) Elected local governance body at district level
(iii) Biannual shift of government between Jammu and Srinagar
(iv) Senior administrative officer heading a revenue division

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Darbar Move = biannual government shift (iii). DDC = elected district-level body (ii). Lt. Governor = head of UT administration (i). Divisional Commissioner = senior officer heading division (iv). '(a)-(ii), (b)-(iii), (c)-(iv), (d)-(i)' swaps (a) and (b). '(a)-(iii), (b)-(i), (c)-(ii), (d)-(iv)' swaps (b) and (c). '(a)-(iv), (b)-(ii), (c)-(i), (d)-(iii)' swaps (a) and (d).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
The following data shows apple production (lakh MT) in J&K:

2019-20 → 17.2
2020-21 → 18.5
2021-22 → 21.2
2022-23 → 19.8

In which year was the year-on-year increase highest?
questions.explanation: 2020-21: 18.5-17.2=1.3. 2021-22: 21.2-18.5=2.7 (highest). 2022-23: 19.8-21.2=-1.4 (decrease). '2020-21' is wrong — increase was only 1.3. '2022-23' is wrong — it was a decrease. '2019-20' is wrong — no prior year data to compare.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Avantipora' ruins in Pulwama district date back to which historical period?
questions.explanation: Avantipora was founded by King Avantivarman (855-883 CE) with temples dedicated to Vishnu and Shiva. 'Mughal period' is wrong — Mughals came much later (16th century). 'Sikh period' is wrong — 19th century. 'Dogra period' is wrong — also 19th century.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the 'Dal Lake' of Srinagar:

(i) It is approximately 18 sq km in area.
(ii) Dal Lake has no connection to any other water body.
(iii) Houseboats and shikaras are iconic features of the lake.
(iv) The floating vegetable gardens ('Rad') are found in Dal Lake.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Dal Lake is ~18 sq km (i correct). Houseboats/shikaras are iconic (ii correct). Floating gardens exist (iii correct). (ii) is wrong because Dal Lake is connected to Nigeen Lake via a narrow channel. '(i), (iii), (iv) and (ii)' includes (ii). '(i) and (iii) only' excludes (iv). '(iii), (iv) and (ii) only' includes (ii).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Zoji La Tunnel' project, when completed, will provide:
options: A railway link to the Kashmir Valley
All-weather connectivity between Srinagar and Leh
A shortcut between Jammu and Srinagar
An alternative route to Vaishno Devi
questions.correctAnswer: All-weather connectivity between Srinagar and Leh
questions.explanation: The Zoji La Tunnel will bypass the snow-bound Zoji La pass, providing year-round Srinagar-Leh connectivity. 'Railway link' is wrong — it's a road tunnel. 'Jammu-Srinagar shortcut' is wrong — that's Banihal/NH-44 route. 'Vaishno Devi route' is wrong — completely different direction.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are major handicraft products of Jammu region (as distinct from Kashmir)?

(i) Basohli paintings
(ii) Calico printing
(iii) Pashmina shawls
(iv) Chappal (leather work) of Rajouri

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Basohli paintings are from Kathua/Jammu (i correct). Calico printing is a Jammu region craft (ii correct). Chappal-making is from Rajouri (iv correct). (iii) is wrong because Pashmina shawls are a KASHMIR craft (woven in Srinagar/central Kashmir). '(i), (ii), (iii) and (iv)' includes (iii). '(i) and (iv) only' excludes (ii). '(ii), (iii) and (iv) only' includes (iii).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The 'Karewa' formations are unique geological features found in the Kashmir Valley.
Reason (R): Karewas are elevated plateaus of lacustrine (ancient lake) deposits consisting of clay, silt, and sand, formed when the Kashmir Valley was a large lake millions of years ago.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Karewas are unique to Kashmir Valley (A correct). They are lacustrine deposits from an ancient lake (R correct and explains their geological origin). 'Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)' is wrong because R explains the formation process. '(A) is correct but (R) is not correct' is wrong because R is geologically correct. '(A) is not correct but (R) is correct' is wrong because A is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Mattan Sun Temple' ruins near Anantnag are from the period of:
questions.explanation: The Martand/Mattan Sun Temple was built by Lalitaditya Muktapida (724-760 CE). 'Zain-ul-Abidin' is wrong — he was a 15th century Sultan. 'Akbar' is wrong — 16th century Mughal. 'Dogra' is wrong — 19th century.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The __________ is the state bird of J&K.
questions.explanation: The Black-necked Crane is J&K's state bird. 'Himalayan Monal' is wrong — it's the state bird of Uttarakhand. 'Kashmir Flycatcher' is wrong — while endemic to Kashmir, it's not the state bird. 'Eurasian Collared Dove' is wrong — a common bird, not the state bird.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Sufi tradition' in Kashmir is primarily associated with which order?
questions.explanation: The Rishi Order, indigenous to Kashmir and founded by Sheikh Noor-ud-din (Nund Rishi), is the predominant Sufi tradition in Kashmir. 'Qadiriyya' is wrong — while present, it's not the primary Kashmir order. 'Chishtiyya' is wrong — more prominent in mainland India. 'Naqshbandiyya' is wrong — present but not the dominant Kashmir tradition.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following districts with their division:

Column I:
(a) Shopian
(b) Samba
(c) Kulgam
(d) Reasi

Column II:
(i) Jammu division
(ii) Kashmir division
(iii) Kashmir division
(iv) Jammu division

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Shopian is in Kashmir division (ii). Samba is in Jammu division (i). Kulgam is in Kashmir division (iii). Reasi is in Jammu division (iv). '(a)-(i), (b)-(ii), (c)-(iv), (d)-(iii)' wrongly puts Shopian in Jammu. '(a)-(ii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(iii)' wrongly puts Kulgam in Jammu. '(a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(ii), (d)-(i)' swaps assignments.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about current events in J&K:

(i) District Development Council (DDC) elections were held in J&K in 2020.
(ii) The J&K Reorganisation Act was passed by Parliament on 5 August 2019.
(iii) Article 370 was abrogated through a Presidential Order and Parliamentary resolution.
(iv) J&K Assembly elections have been held every year since 2019.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — DDC elections were held in November–December 2020. (ii) is correct — the J&K Reorganisation Bill was passed by Parliament on 5-6 August 2019. (iii) is correct — Article 370 was rendered inoperative through a Presidential Order together with a resolution of Parliament. (iv) is wrong — Assembly elections have not been held annually; there was a single UT Assembly election, in September–October 2024, after which Omar Abdullah became Chief Minister on 16 October 2024. The option listing all four includes (iv); '(i) and (iii) only' drops the correct (ii); and '(ii), (iii) and (iv) only' again includes (iv).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Chenab Bridge on the USBRL project holds which world record?
questions.explanation: The Chenab Bridge carries the railway about 359 metres above the Chenab riverbed in Reasi district, making it the world's highest railway arch bridge; it was inaugurated on 6 June 2025 as part of the 272 km USBRL. Note that the Anji Khad Bridge is a different bridge on the same line — India's first cable-stayed railway bridge. 'World's longest railway bridge' is wrong — that record lies elsewhere and the Chenab Bridge's claim is height, not length. 'World's deepest bridge foundation' is wrong — not a record it holds. 'World's widest single-span bridge' is wrong — its distinction is height above the riverbed, not deck width.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
The following data shows the number of tourists (in lakhs) visiting famous destinations in J&K in a year:

Vaishno Devi → 85
Gulmarg → 12
Pahalgam → 8
Dal Lake/Srinagar → 45
Patnitop → 5

What percentage of total tourists visit Vaishno Devi?
questions.explanation: Total = 85+12+8+45+5 = 155 lakhs. Vaishno Devi % = (85/155)×100 ≈ 54.8%. '45%' is wrong — that would need 69.75 out of 155. '60%' is wrong — would need 93 out of 155. '50%' is wrong — would need 77.5 out of 155.
